description: Default-deny capability for the main window — no fs:, no bare shell:, only core defaults, the narrow dialog:allow-open grant for the project registration folder picker (T-01-02), and a shell:allow-execute grant scoped to exactly one named sidecar binary (T-02-01/T-02-09). The renderer has no shell capability; only the Rust core's sidecar supervisor (src-tauri/src/sidecar.rs) invokes tauri-plugin-shell. Tauri v2's ACL gates PLUGIN commands only; this app's own #[tauri::command] handlers are exposed solely through main.rs's generate_handler! list, which is the enforcement point (tests/handler_roster.rs pins it). The window is granted NO permission from the notification plugin: the Rust core alone shows banners (D-175). App-command roster, kept here for auditability: project_register, project_list, project_reconcile, project_relocate, project_hide, project_restore, milestone_create, milestone_list, milestone_set_state, epic_create, epic_list, epic_update, epic_set_state, story_create, story_list, story_get, story_context_packet_size, story_update, story_set_state, story_write_by_hand, story_list_for_project, criterion_create, criterion_list, criterion_amend, criterion_accept, criterion_unaccept, criterion_delete, check_set, check_remove, task_add, task_list, task_set_state, task_rename, task_move, proposal_list_pending, proposal_accept, proposal_reject, actor_list, events_activity_trail, events_since_cursor, menu_set_action_enabled, session_start, story_start, story_resume, story_stopped, story_drop, session_log_window, session_raw_window, sessions_for_story, story_session_summaries, session_acknowledge, session_acknowledge_many, worktree_summary, worktree_remove_check, worktree_remove, worktree_recreate, worktree_forget_record, session_stop, session_discard, session_answer_permission, permission_rules_list, permission_rule_revoke, session_pending_permissions, story_latest_session, board_blocked_summary, board_recovery_summary, sessions_pending_orphans, orphan_kill, settings_get, settings_set_credential_mode, settings_store_api_key, settings_clear_api_key, backend_capability_probe, settings_set_notifications_enabled, git_identifier_resolve, git_facts, git_truth_focus_story, worktree_open, open_command_template, set_open_command_template, fleet_list, fleet_blocked_queue, fleet_watch_run, worktree_inventory, worktree_measure, worktree_reclaim. Every handler resolves the actor server-side (T-01-04) and accepts ids and plain values only; no path, ref, sha or actor crosses IPC. The record commands follow GLOSSARY.md (Milestone, Epic, Story, Acceptance criterion, Check, Task as the Story checklist, Proposal); criterion_accept/criterion_unaccept, check_set/check_remove and proposal_accept/proposal_reject are human-only, enforced again inside packages/core by reading the actor's type in the write transaction. worktree_remove and worktree_reclaim re-read the worktree's porcelain status inside packages/core and refuse on any uncommitted change; no parameter can skip that guard. Reads cap their windows server-side.
